_meta.source: MOE post secondary admissions pages, MOE press release on ITE upgrader admissions to polytechnics from AY2027, ITE and polytechnic progression pages
_meta.notes: The onward edges of the system. Every destination must have at least one, which is what makes a dead end impossible to render. The honest field is never cut: it is the credibility of the whole route system.

routes.label: Poly, then university
routes.detail: Diplomas carry exemptions, so a degree often starts in Year 2.
routes.honest: Competitive. Your diploma GPA counts most.

routes.label: ITE, then poly
routes.detail: Finish Higher Nitec at GPA 2.5 to apply. A raw 3.5 guarantees a place.
routes.honest: About two years longer than going straight.

routes.label: ITE, poly, then a degree
routes.detail: Longer, and each step gives you a full qualification.
routes.honest: Longer. You can work part time along the way.

routes.label: Nitec, then Higher Nitec
routes.detail: Start at Year 1 of the same 3 year course. Same certificate at the end.

routes.label: Foundation year, then poly
routes.detail: A year inside the polytechnic, then straight into Year 1.
routes.honest: The diploma is the same as everyone else's.

routes.label: A fifth year, then JC
routes.detail: One more year at a harder level, then the JC route on that.
routes.honest: One year longer than going straight to JC.

routes.label: A fifth year, then poly
routes.detail: The most common reason to take a fifth year.
routes.honest: Useful when you are aiming at one course.

routes.label: Work and study together
routes.detail: SkillsFuture Work Study runs at Certificate, Diploma and Degree level, and it pays.
routes.honest: Demanding: a job and a course at the same time.

routes.label: A degree later
routes.detail: SUSS and SIT run part time and applied degrees built for working adults.
routes.honest: Most people who take this route start after age 30.
